title: Control menopausal hot flashes through neurokinin-3 receptor blockade

concept.text: Treat moderate-to-severe menopausal vasomotor symptoms through targeted non-hormonal pharmacology. Fezolinetant established this class; subsequent recognition of serious liver-injury risk qualifies its clinical use. Proposed completion test: FDA approval of an NK3 antagonist for menopausal vasomotor symptoms, supported by randomized phase 3 evidence of reduced hot-flash frequency and severity through 12 weeks and longer safety follow-up. Test set by: FDA; pivotal efficacy and safety endpoints were evaluated in the fezolinetant programme. Reported achieved: FDA approved fezolinetant (Veozah) on 12 May 2023; a boxed liver-injury warning was added on 16 December 2024. Overlaps: OBG-05, END-08. Sources given: [FDA fezolinetant approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-novel-drug-treat-moderate-severe-hot-flashes-caused-menopause) ; [FDA subsequent liver-injury warning](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-communications/fda-adds-warning-about-rare-occurrence-serious-liver-injury-use-veozah-fezolinetant-hot-flashes-due).

page.title: First NK3 receptor antagonist for menopausal vasomotor symptoms
page.definition: An oral nonhormonal drug blocks neurokinin-3 (NK3) receptors, which participate in the brain’s temperature regulation, and reduces moderate-to-severe menopausal vasomotor symptoms: hot flashes and night sweats.

goal.need: Women who cannot use hormone therapy because of contraindications, or who decline it, need nonhormonal symptom relief. Vasomotor symptoms persist for more than 10 years in one-third of women.

figures.caption: Frequency and duration of menopausal vasomotor symptoms
figures.note: Estimates summarized in the society’s 2023 position statement.

statements.quote: Nonhormone options are important considerations for women who are not good candidates for HT.
Hot flashes as a result of menopause can be a serious physical burden on women and impact their quality of life

completion.title: FDA approves an NK3 receptor antagonist for moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause.
completion.criterion: The US Food and Drug Administration approves a neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor antagonist, a drug class that includes fezolinetant, for the treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause. The approval rests on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials with 12-week controlled periods. The first such approval was Veozah (fezolinetant) 45 mg tablets once daily on 12 May 2023: 1,022 women averaging at least 7 moderate to severe episodes per day were randomized, and frequency and severity fell more than with placebo at weeks 4 and 12, frequency by at least 2 episodes per day more.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, approval of NDA 216578, Veozah prescribing information and news release of 12 May 2023.
completion.threshold_quote: Veozah is the first neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor antagonist approved by the FDA to treat moderate to severe hot flashes from menopause.
completion.basis: The breakthrough is the first approval of a drug class, and the FDA states it as a first, so the test names that event with its indication and pivotal trials. FDA added a boxed warning for rare serious liver injury on 16 December 2024; the approval stands, with liver tests before and during treatment. The test does not cover vasomotor symptoms caused by endocrine therapy for cancer, or efficacy beyond the 12-week controlled periods.

milestones.title: An NK3 antagonist has nonclinical evidence supporting human dosing.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacology and toxicology support a conclusion that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe, considering its dose and duration. Fezolinetant inhibited human NK3-receptor signalling with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations of 12.9–22.0 nmol/L. FDA reviewed its 13-week rat and monkey toxicity studies on 31 May 2016; its review dated 1 July 2019 accepted 26-week rat and 39-week monkey studies as supporting the proposed phase 3 duration.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8); application to fezolinetant documented in the NDA 216578 nonclinical review.
milestones.threshold_quote: reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: An NK3 antagonist reduces hot-flash counts versus placebo after 4 weeks at two-sided P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate superiority on the registered primary endpoint: total hot flashes during the final week of each 4-week treatment period, using a randomized, double-blind crossover comparison with placebo and a 2-week washout. In the 2017 MLE4901 report, 37 women contributed to the intention-to-treat analysis and 28 completed both periods. MLE4901 40 mg twice daily reduced adjusted weekly counts by 29.66 versus placebo (95% CI 17.39–42.87; P<0.0001).
milestones.set_by: Imperial College London, protocol MR/M024954/1, registered as EudraCT 2015-001553-32 and NCT02668185.
milestones.threshold_quote: Total Number of Hot Flushes During the Final Week of Both Treatment Periods.

milestones.title: A dose-ranging trial finds an NK3-antagonist regimen improving all four hot-flash endpoints at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: In a 12-week randomized placebo-controlled dose-ranging trial, a regimen reduces moderate-to-severe hot-flash frequency and severity at weeks 4 and 12, using two-sided 5% pairwise tests without multiplicity adjustment. Severity is the count-weighted mean of scores 2 (moderate) and 3 (severe). VESTA randomized 356 women; 352 received treatment and 349 entered the efficacy analysis. Fezolinetant 60 mg once daily and 60 or 90 mg twice daily met all four comparisons.
milestones.set_by: OGEDA/Astellas, VESTA protocol NCT03192176; endpoints and statistical tests reproduced in the published phase 2b report.
milestones.threshold_quote: using a two-sided test at 5% error rate without the multiplicity adjustment.

milestones.title: Two phase 3 trials show at least 2 fewer daily hot flashes than placebo at weeks 4 and 12.
milestones.criterion: In each of two randomized placebo-controlled trials, show reductions in frequency and severity at weeks 4 and 12 using multiplicity-adjusted testing at the 0.05 level; frequency must fall by ≥2 moderate-to-severe episodes/day more than placebo at both visits. On-treatment severity is the count-weighted mean of mild=1, moderate=2 and severe=3. Fezolinetant 45 mg daily met this test in SKYLIGHT 1 (527 randomized) and SKYLIGHT 2 (501 randomized). Week-12 reductions beyond placebo were 2.55 and 2.53 episodes/day, respectively.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, development advice and NDA 216578 statistical review; statistical significance level documented in the approved prescribing information.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least 14 moderate to severe VMS per week or 2 moderate to severe VMS per day

milestones.title: An NK3 antagonist meets the 12-month endometrial limit: ≤1% hyperplasia, upper one-sided 95% CI ≤4%.
milestones.criterion: After 12 months, biopsy-assessed endometrial hyperplasia (overgrowth of the uterine lining) occurs in ≤1% of treated women, with an upper one-sided 95% confidence limit ≤4%. SKYLIGHT 4 treated 1,830 women for up to 52 weeks. Among 203 evaluable women assigned fezolinetant 45 mg daily, one had hyperplasia (0.5%; upper confidence limit 2.3%) and none had endometrial malignancy.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 2003 draft guidance §IV.E–F, originally written for estrogen/progestin products and applied in SKYLIGHT 4. Numerical bounds also appear in Veozah prescribing information §14.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: ≤ 1% with the upper bound of the one-sided 95% confidence limit being ≤ 4%.

results.finding: Fezolinetant nonclinical studies (sample sizes not stated), including 39-week monkey toxicity testing, supported the proposed phase 3 duration.
results.detail: FDA's review dated 1 July 2019 accepted the rat and monkey studies as supporting phase 3 duration and adequately addressing the major human metabolite. The NDA pharmacology/toxicology review also supported approval.

results.finding: MLE4901 reduced adjusted weekly hot-flash counts by 29.66 versus placebo in 37 women in the intention-to-treat analysis.
results.detail: Randomized, double-blind crossover trial of 40 mg twice daily, with 4-week treatment periods and a 2-week washout; 28 completed both periods. The registered primary endpoint was met (95% CI 17.39–42.87; two-sided P<0.0001).

results.detail: The 12-week randomized, double-blind dose-ranging trial used two-sided 5% pairwise tests without multiplicity adjustment. Frequency and count-weighted moderate/severe symptom severity improved at weeks 4 and 12.

results.finding: VESTA fezolinetant: 352 treated participants; no clinically significant endometrial biopsy findings during 12 weeks.
results.detail: Endometrial safety was assessed, but treatment lasted only 12 weeks. The source provides neither an evaluable biopsy denominator nor a hyperplasia confidence limit establishing the required 12-month threshold.
results.quote: There were no clinically significant endometrial biopsy findings and no meaningful changes from baseline or compared with placebo in endometrial thickness measured by transvaginal ultrasound

results.finding: SKYLIGHT 1 (527 randomized): fezolinetant 45 mg daily reduced hot-flash frequency by 2.55 episodes/day more than placebo at week 12.
results.detail: The 45 mg dose exceeded placebo by 2.07 episodes/day at week 4; frequency and severity improved significantly at both visits with multiplicity control. This source reports one qualifying phase 3 trial; the criterion requires two.
results.quote:
At week 12, the difference 
in the change in least squares mean compared with 
placebo was –2·39 (0·44; p<0·001) for fezolinetant 
30 mg and –2·55 (0·43; p<0·001) for fezolinetant 45 mg.

results.finding: SKYLIGHT 1: among 173 women receiving fezolinetant 45 mg, zero endometrial hyperplasia, cancer, or disordered proliferative endometrium adverse events were reported through 12 weeks.
results.detail: Table 3 reports short-term adverse events, not the required 12-month biopsy-assessed hyperplasia incidence. No evaluable biopsy denominator or upper one-sided 95% confidence limit is supplied.

results.finding: SKYLIGHT 2 (501 randomized): fezolinetant 45 mg daily reduced hot-flash frequency by 2.53 episodes/day more than placebo at week 12.
results.detail: The week-4 difference was 2.55 episodes/day; frequency and severity improved at both visits with multiplicity adjustment. This report establishes results for only one of the two required phase 3 trials; SKYLIGHT 1 is discussed but its qualifying results are not reported.
results.quote: Both fezolinetant doses met statistical significance in reducing VMS frequency and severity/24 hours at weeks 4 and 12 vs placebo with multiplicity adjustment

results.finding: SKYLIGHT 2: among 167 women assigned fezolinetant 45 mg, zero endometrial hyperplasia/cancer or disordered proliferative endometrium events were reported through week 52.
results.detail: Table 6 reports a composite adverse-event outcome using the safety population. It does not provide the 12-month evaluable-biopsy denominator or upper one-sided 95% confidence limit needed to establish the endometrial safety criterion.

results.finding: SKYLIGHT 4: fezolinetant 45 mg daily yielded 0.5% endometrial hyperplasia among 203 evaluable women.
results.detail: After 52 weeks, the upper one-sided 95% confidence limit was 2.3%, satisfying both limits. The trial treated 1,830 women; endometrial biopsies were assessed by blinded independent pathologists.
results.quote: In the fezolinetant 45-mg group, 1 of 203 participants had endometrial hyperplasia (0.5%; upper limit of one-sided 95% CI 2.3%); there were no cases in the placebo (0/186) or fezolinetant 30 mg (0/210) group.
